herod_1504.name: Herod
herod_1504.who: King of Judea when Jesus was born, who tried to kill the child Jesus.
key: Zechariah served as a priest in the days of Herod, king of Judea (Luke 1).
Wise men from the east came to Jerusalem asking Herod where the newborn king of the Jews was (Matthew 2).
Herod secretly asked the wise men to report the child's location so he could supposedly worship him (Matthew 2).
Tricked by the wise men, he ordered all boys two and under in Bethlehem killed (Matthew 2).
After Herod died, Joseph brought Jesus back from Egypt, avoiding Herod's son Archelaus (Matthew 2).

izhar_658.name: Izhar
izhar_658.who: Levite son of Kohath and father of Korah, ancestor of the Izharite clan.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, with sons Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri (Exodus 6).
The Izharites were one of the Kohathite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).
His son Korah led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
David organized his descendants, led by Shelomith, among the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).

kedar_1769.name: Kedar
kedar_1769.who: Second son of Ishmael, whose descendants became a prominent Arabian tribe known by his name.
key: He was born the second son of Ishmael, one of twelve princes from Ishmael (Genesis 25).
Solomon's song compares the beloved's dark beauty to the tents of Kedar (Song of Solomon 1).
Isaiah foretold that all the glory of Kedar would come to an end (Isaiah 21).
Isaiah pictured the flocks of Kedar gathered to honor the LORD in Zion (Isaiah 60).
Jeremiah prophesied that Nebuchadnezzar would strike Kedar (Jeremiah 49).

mark_1679.name: Mark
mark_1679.who: Early Christian worker, cousin of Barnabas, who served alongside Paul, Barnabas, and Peter.
key: After his release from prison, Peter went to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark (Acts 12).
He assisted Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus but left them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13).
Paul and Barnabas parted over taking him again, and Barnabas took him to Cyprus (Acts 15).
Paul later named Mark, Barnabas's cousin, among his fellow workers (Colossians 4).
Paul asked Timothy to bring Mark, calling him useful for ministry (2 Timothy 4).

nahor_2143.name: Nahor
nahor_2143.who: Brother of Abraham who settled in Mesopotamia; grandfather of Rebekah and Laban.
key: He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran (Genesis 11).
Abraham heard that Milcah and the concubine Reumah had borne Nahor many children (Genesis 22).
Abraham's servant found Rebekah, Nahor's granddaughter, at the city of Nahor (Genesis 24).
Jacob met shepherds who knew Laban, whom they called the son of Nahor (Genesis 29).
Laban and Jacob swore a covenant before the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor (Genesis 31).

neriah_2186.name: Neriah
neriah_2186.who: Son of Mahseiah and father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, and of Seraiah, a royal officer.
key: Jeremiah gave his land deed to Baruch the son of Neriah for safekeeping (Jeremiah 32).
Baruch the son of Neriah wrote Jeremiah's prophecies on a scroll and read them aloud (Jeremiah 36).
Leaders accused Baruch the son of Neriah of turning Jeremiah against them (Jeremiah 43).
Jeremiah gave a personal word from the LORD to Baruch the son of Neriah (Jeremiah 45).
Seraiah the son of Neriah carried Jeremiah's prophecy against Babylon to that city (Jeremiah 51).

sanballat_2470.name: Sanballat
sanballat_2470.who: Sanballat the Horonite, a leading opponent of Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
key: He was displeased that Nehemiah came to seek the welfare of Israel, and mocked the work (Nehemiah 2).
He ridiculed the builders and plotted with others to attack Jerusalem (Nehemiah 4).
He repeatedly tried to lure Nehemiah away and sent an open letter accusing him of rebellion (Nehemiah 6).
A grandson of the high priest Eliashib became his son-in-law, so Nehemiah drove him away (Nehemiah 13).

seth_2504.name: Seth
seth_2504.who: Son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's murder, through whom the line to Noah continued.
key: Eve bore Seth, saying God had appointed another offspring in place of Abel (Genesis 4).
After his son Enosh was born, people began to call on the LORD's name (Genesis 4).
He fathered Enosh at 105 and lived 912 years in all (Genesis 5).
He is listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the son of Adam (Luke 3).

simon_2750.name: Simon Iscariot
simon_2750.who: Father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus; he is known only through his son.
key: Jesus said one of the Twelve was a devil, meaning Judas the son of Simon Iscariot (John 6).
The devil put it into the heart of Judas, Simon's son, to betray Jesus (John 13).
Jesus gave a morsel of bread to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, identifying the betrayer (John 13).

terah_2841.name: Terah
terah_2841.who: Father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who led his family from Ur toward Canaan.
key: He fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran (Genesis 11).
He took Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur toward Canaan but settled in Haran (Genesis 11).
He died in Haran at the age of 205 (Genesis 11).
Joshua recalled that Terah lived beyond the Euphrates and served other gods (Joshua 24).
He is listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).

vashti_2937.name: Vashti
vashti_2937.who: Queen of Persia, wife of King Ahasuerus, removed after refusing his summons during a royal feast.
key: She gave a feast for the women in King Ahasuerus's palace (Esther 1).
She refused the king's command to come and display her beauty before his guests (Esther 1).
On his officials' advice, the king decreed that she lose her royal position (Esther 1).
The search for a queen to replace Vashti led to Esther's selection (Esther 2).

abel_13.name: Abel
abel_13.who: Second son of Adam and Eve, a shepherd whose offering God accepted, murdered by his brother Cain.
key: A keeper of sheep, he offered firstborn of his flock, and the LORD regarded his offering (Genesis 4).
His brother Cain killed him in the field (Genesis 4).
Jesus spoke of the blood of righteous Abel in warning the scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23).
By faith he offered God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain (Hebrews 11).
Jesus' sprinkled blood is said to speak a better word than Abel's blood (Hebrews 12).

beor_466.name: Beor
beor_466.who: Father of Balaam, the diviner hired by Balak king of Moab to curse Israel.
key: Balak sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel (Numbers 22).
Balaam the son of Beor blessed Israel instead of cursing them (Numbers 24).
Israel killed Balaam the son of Beor in the war against Midian (Numbers 31).
Peter warned of false teachers following the way of Balaam the son of Beor (2 Peter 2).

bethuel_487.name: Bethuel
bethuel_487.who: Son of Nahor and Milcah, nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah and Laban.
key: He was born to Nahor and Milcah and became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22).
With Laban, he agreed that Rebekah's marriage to Isaac came from the LORD (Genesis 24).
Rebekah is called the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram (Genesis 25).
Isaac sent Jacob to Bethuel's house to take a wife from Laban's daughters (Genesis 28).

caiaphas_532.name: Caiaphas
caiaphas_532.who: High priest during Jesus' ministry, son-in-law of Annas, who led the council's case against Jesus.
key: He was high priest, alongside Annas, when John the Baptist began preaching (Luke 3).
He said it was better for one man to die for the people, which John calls prophecy (John 11).
Chief priests met in his palace to plot Jesus' arrest (Matthew 26).
At Jesus' trial he demanded whether Jesus was the Christ, then tore his robes (Matthew 26).
With Annas and others, he questioned Peter and John after a lame man was healed (Acts 4).

deborah_997.name: Deborah
deborah_997.who: Prophetess and judge of Israel who summoned Barak to defeat Sisera's Canaanite army.
key: As a prophetess and wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel under a palm tree (Judges 4).
She summoned Barak and relayed God's command to fight Sisera at Mount Tabor (Judges 4).
She went with Barak, saying the LORD would sell Sisera into a woman's hand (Judges 4).
She and Barak sang a song praising the LORD for the victory (Judges 5).
Afterward the land had rest for forty years (Judges 5).

eliakim_1084.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1084.who: Son of Hilkiah, royal household administrator for King Hezekiah during the Assyrian threat.
key: Isaiah foretold that God would place Eliakim over the royal household in place of Shebna (Isaiah 22).
He went out to meet the Rabshakeh and asked him to speak Aramaic, not Hebrew (2 Kings 18).
He reported the Assyrian threats to Hezekiah with his clothes torn (2 Kings 18).
Hezekiah sent him, clothed in sackcloth, to seek a word from Isaiah (2 Kings 19).

gaal_1259.name: Gaal
gaal_1259.who: Son of Ebed, who stirred Shechem to revolt against Abimelech and was defeated and driven out.
key: He moved into Shechem with his relatives, and its leaders put their trust in him (Judges 9).
At a festival he boasted he would remove Abimelech if the people were under him (Judges 9).
Zebul, the city's ruler, secretly warned Abimelech about Gaal's challenge (Judges 9).
Abimelech defeated him, and Zebul drove Gaal and his relatives out of Shechem (Judges 9).

hivite_1534.name: Hivites
hivite_1534.who: A Canaanite people descended from Canaan.

jonadab_799.name: Jonadab
jonadab_799.who: Son of Rechab who supported Jehu against Baal worship and gave his descendants strict rules of life.
key: Jehu took him into his chariot to see his zeal for the LORD (2 Kings 10).
He went with Jehu into the house of Baal before Baal's worshipers were destroyed (2 Kings 10).
His descendants, the Rechabites, still obeyed his command not to drink wine (Jeremiah 35).
God promised Jonadab would never lack a man to stand before him (Jeremiah 35).

laadan_1823.name: Ladan
laadan_1823.who: Levite son of Gershon whose descendants served in the tabernacle and temple.
key: As Libni, he is listed among the sons of Gershon, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Libnites were a Gershonite clan who served at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).
David organized his sons Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel among the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His descendants were placed over the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).

pharaoh_2332.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2332.who: King of Egypt in Solomon's day, who gave his daughter to Solomon in marriage.
key: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh and married his daughter (1 Kings 3).
Pharaoh captured Gezer and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife (1 Kings 9).
He gave Hadad the Edomite the sister of his wife Tahpenes in marriage (1 Kings 11).
Solomon moved Pharaoh's daughter into a house he built for her (2 Chronicles 8).

rezin_2435.name: Rezin
rezin_2435.who: King of Syria at Damascus who allied with Pekah of Israel against King Ahaz of Judah.
key: The LORD began sending Rezin and Pekah against Judah (2 Kings 15).
Rezin and Pekah besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem but could not conquer him (2 Kings 16).
Isaiah told Ahaz not to fear Rezin and the son of Remaliah (Isaiah 7).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured Damascus and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16).

zacharias_2971.name: Zechariah
zacharias_2971.who: Priest and father of John the Baptist, made mute for doubting Gabriel's announcement of his son's birth.
key: He was a righteous priest of the division of Abijah, and his wife Elizabeth was barren (Luke 1).
Gabriel announced John's birth in the temple, and Zechariah was made mute for not believing (Luke 1).
At the naming he wrote that the child's name was John, and his speech returned (Luke 1).
Filled with the Holy Spirit, he prophesied about God's salvation and John's calling (Luke 1).
The word of God later came to his son John in the wilderness (Luke 3).

zalmunna_2983.name: Zalmunna
zalmunna_2983.who: King of Midian who, with Zebah, was pursued, captured, and executed by Gideon.
key: Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, across the Jordan (Judges 8).
The men of Succoth and Penuel refused bread to Gideon's pursuing troops (Judges 8).
Gideon routed their army at Karkor and captured both kings (Judges 8).
After they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, Gideon killed them (Judges 8).
A psalm asks God to make Israel's enemies like Zebah and Zalmunna (Psalm 83).

zebah_2997.name: Zebah
zebah_2997.who: King of Midian who, with Zalmunna, was pursued, captured, and executed by Gideon.
key: Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, across the Jordan (Judges 8).
The men of Succoth and Penuel refused bread to Gideon's pursuing troops (Judges 8).
Gideon routed their army at Karkor and captured both kings (Judges 8).
After they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, Gideon killed them (Judges 8).
A psalm asks God to make Israel's enemies like Zebah and Zalmunna (Psalm 83).

zelophehad_3035.name: Zelophehad
zelophehad_3035.who: Manassite son of Hepher who died without sons, whose five daughters won the right to inherit.
key: He is listed as having no sons, only five daughters (Numbers 26).
His daughters asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the LORD granted it (Numbers 27).
His daughters said he died in the wilderness for his own sin, not with Korah (Numbers 27).
His daughters were told to marry within their father's tribe to keep the inheritance (Numbers 36).
His daughters received land among the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17).

abiram_47.name: Abiram
abiram_47.who: Reubenite son of Eliab who, with his brother Dathan, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses.
key: With Dathan and Korah, he rose up against the leadership of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
He and Dathan refused Moses' summons, accusing him of failing to bring them to the promised land (Numbers 16).
The earth opened and swallowed him, his household, and the other rebels (Numbers 16).
Moses reminded Israel of what God did to Dathan and Abiram (Deuteronomy 11).
A psalm recalls the earth swallowing Dathan and covering Abiram's company (Psalm 106).

anak_252.name: Anak
anak_252.who: Son of Arba and ancestor of the Anakim, the tall people of Hebron who frightened Israel's spies.
key: The spies saw descendants of Anak at Hebron and felt like grasshoppers beside them (Numbers 13).
Moses assured Israel that God would defeat the sons of Anak before them (Deuteronomy 9).
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, from Hebron (Joshua 15).
Kiriath-arba, named for Anak's father, was given to the priests as a city of refuge (Joshua 21).

belshazzar_437.name: Belshazzar
belshazzar_437.who: King of Babylon who misused the temple vessels and was killed the night the handwriting appeared.
key: Daniel received a vision of four beasts in Belshazzar's first year (Daniel 7).
Daniel saw the vision of the ram and goat in Belshazzar's third year (Daniel 8).
At a great feast he drank from the gold vessels taken from God's temple (Daniel 5).
A hand wrote on the wall, and Daniel interpreted it as God's judgment (Daniel 5).
That very night Belshazzar was killed, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom (Daniel 5).

bezaleel_490.name: Bezalel
bezaleel_490.who: Craftsman of Judah, son of Uri, whom God filled with his Spirit to build the tabernacle.
key: God called Bezalel by name and filled him with skill for all craftsmanship (Exodus 31).
Moses announced his calling and said God had given him ability to teach (Exodus 35).
He and Oholiab led the skilled workers in making the tabernacle (Exodus 36).
He made the ark of the covenant, its mercy seat, and the cherubim (Exodus 37).
Solomon sought the LORD at the bronze altar Bezalel had made (2 Chronicles 1).

bichri_493.name: Bichri
bichri_493.who: Benjaminite, father of Sheba, who led a revolt against King David.
key: His son Sheba blew a trumpet and called Israel to abandon David (2 Samuel 20).
The head of Sheba the son of Bichri was thrown to Joab from Abel's wall (2 Samuel 20).

darius_980.name: Darius the Mede
darius_980.who: Median ruler who received Babylon's kingdom and was forced by his own decree to cast Daniel to lions.
key: At about sixty-two years old he received the kingdom after Belshazzar's death (Daniel 5).
He set 120 satraps over the kingdom, with Daniel among three officials over them (Daniel 6).
Tricked into signing a decree, he had Daniel thrown into the lions' den (Daniel 6).
Overjoyed at Daniel's rescue, he decreed that all should fear Daniel's God (Daniel 6).
In his first year, Daniel studied Jeremiah's prophecy and prayed for his people (Daniel 9).

dathan_982.name: Dathan
dathan_982.who: Reubenite son of Eliab who, with his brother Abiram, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses.
key: With Abiram and Korah, he rose up against the leadership of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
He and Abiram refused Moses' summons, accusing him of failing to bring them to the promised land (Numbers 16).
The earth opened and swallowed him, his household, and the other rebels (Numbers 16).
Moses reminded Israel of what God did to Dathan and Abiram (Deuteronomy 11).
A psalm recalls the earth opening and swallowing Dathan (Psalm 106).

dinah_1012.name: Dinah
dinah_1012.who: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, whose violation by Shechem led her brothers to take violent revenge.
key: Leah bore her to Jacob after six sons (Genesis 30).
Shechem, son of Hamor, seized and violated her, then sought to marry her (Genesis 34).
Her brothers Simeon and Levi killed the men of Shechem in revenge (Genesis 34).
She went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).

ehud_1039.name: Ehud
ehud_1039.who: Left-handed Benjaminite judge who killed Eglon king of Moab and delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.
key: After Israel served Eglon eighteen years, the LORD raised up Ehud as a deliverer (Judges 3).
He brought Israel's tribute to Eglon and killed him with a hidden double-edged sword (Judges 3).
He rallied Israel, seized the Jordan fords, and struck down about ten thousand Moabites (Judges 3).
The land then had rest for eighty years (Judges 3).
After Ehud died, Israel again did evil in the LORD's sight (Judges 4).

eliphaz_1144.name: Eliphaz
eliphaz_1144.who: Firstborn son of Esau by Adah, whose descendants became chiefs of Edom.
key: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau in Canaan (Genesis 36).
His sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz (Genesis 36).
His concubine Timna bore him Amalek (Genesis 36).
His sons became chiefs in the land of Edom (Genesis 36).
He and his sons are listed again in the genealogy of Esau (1 Chronicles 1).

elisabeth_1152.name: Elizabeth
elisabeth_1152.who: Wife of the priest Zechariah and relative of Mary, who bore John the Baptist in old age.
key: A righteous descendant of Aaron, she was barren and advanced in years (Luke 1).
After conceiving, she kept herself hidden for five months (Luke 1).
When Mary greeted her, her baby leaped, and she blessed Mary by the Holy Spirit (Luke 1).
At his naming she insisted that her son be called John (Luke 1).

enos_1193.name: Enosh
enos_1193.who: Son of Seth and grandson of Adam, in whose days people began to call on the LORD's name.
key: After Seth's son Enosh was born, people began to call on the LORD's name (Genesis 4).
He fathered Kenan at ninety and lived 905 years in all (Genesis 5).
He is listed in the genealogy from Adam (1 Chronicles 1).
He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the son of Seth (Luke 3).

felix_1257.name: Felix
felix_1257.who: Roman governor of Judea who heard Paul's case at Caesarea and kept him imprisoned two years.
key: The tribune Lysias sent Paul to Governor Felix at Caesarea with a letter (Acts 23).
He heard Tertullus accuse Paul and heard Paul's defense, then postponed a decision (Acts 24).
With his wife Drusilla he heard Paul, and grew alarmed at talk of coming judgment (Acts 24).
Hoping for a bribe, he kept Paul in custody two years until Festus succeeded him (Acts 24).

gog_1326.name: Gog
gog_1326.who: Ruler from the land of Magog whom Ezekiel foresaw attacking Israel in the latter days.
key: Ezekiel prophesied against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
God declared he would bring Gog against Israel in the latter years, then judge him (Ezekiel 38).
Gog's armies would fall on Israel's mountains and be buried in a valley (Ezekiel 39).
After the thousand years, Satan gathers Gog and Magog for battle, and fire consumes them (Revelation 20).

hananiah_1395.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1395.who: False prophet from Gibeon who opposed Jeremiah by promising a quick end to Babylon's rule.
key: In the temple he claimed God would break Babylon's yoke within two years (Jeremiah 28).
He took the yoke bars from Jeremiah's neck and broke them (Jeremiah 28).
Jeremiah declared that the LORD had not sent him and that he would die that year (Jeremiah 28).
Hananiah died in the seventh month of that same year (Jeremiah 28).

hanun_1404.name: Hanun
hanun_1404.who: Ammonite king, son of Nahash, who humiliated David's envoys and provoked war with Israel.
key: When he succeeded his father Nahash, David sent servants to console him (2 Samuel 10).
Suspecting spies, he shaved off half their beards and cut their garments (2 Samuel 10).
He hired Syrian troops, but Joab and Abishai defeated the Ammonites and Syrians (2 Samuel 10).
He sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots against David (1 Chronicles 19).

hebron_1475.name: Hebron
hebron_1475.who: Levite son of Kohath, ancestor of the Hebronite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Hebronites were one of the Kohathite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).
Eliel led eighty of Hebron's descendants in bringing the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15).
His sons Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam are listed in David's Levite divisions (1 Chronicles 23).

hoshea_1559.name: Hoshea
hoshea_1559.who: Son of Elah and last king of the northern kingdom of Israel, which fell to Assyria.
key: He conspired against King Pekah, killed him, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
He became Assyria's vassal, then sought help from Egypt and was imprisoned (2 Kings 17).
Assyria besieged Samaria three years, captured it, and carried Israel into exile (2 Kings 17).
Samaria fell in Hoshea's ninth year, during Hezekiah's reign in Judah (2 Kings 18).

jehoahaz_2516.name: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz_2516.who: Son of Josiah who reigned three months over Judah before Pharaoh Neco deposed him and took him to Egypt.
key: The people of the land made him king after Josiah's death (2 Kings 23).
He did evil and reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah (2 Kings 23).
Neco took him to Egypt, where he died (2 Kings 23).
Jeremiah declared that Shallum would never return to his homeland (Jeremiah 22).

jeshua_895.name: Jeshua
jeshua_895.who: Levite leader after the exile who helped rebuild the temple and teach the Law in Ezra and Nehemiah's day.
key: Levites of the family of Jeshua and Kadmiel returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Jeshua and his sons supervised the workmen rebuilding the temple (Ezra 3).
He helped the people understand the Law as Ezra read it (Nehemiah 8).
He led the Levites in calling the people to bless the LORD (Nehemiah 9).
Jeshua the son of Azaniah sealed the covenant to keep God's law (Nehemiah 10).

joash_1630.name: Joash
joash_1630.who: Abiezrite of Ophrah, father of Gideon, who defended his son after Gideon tore down Baal's altar.
key: The angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon under the terebinth at Ophrah belonging to Joash (Judges 6).
When the town demanded Gideon's death, Joash said Baal should contend for himself (Judges 6).
A Midianite's dream spoke of the sword of Gideon the son of Joash (Judges 7).
Gideon was buried in the tomb of his father Joash at Ophrah (Judges 8).

kadmiel_1767.name: Kadmiel
kadmiel_1767.who: Levite family head who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and served in temple rebuilding and worship.
key: Levites of the family of Jeshua and Kadmiel returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Kadmiel and his sons helped supervise the workmen rebuilding the temple (Ezra 3).
He was among the Levites who led the people in praise and confession (Nehemiah 9).
He sealed the covenant to keep God's law (Nehemiah 10).

maachah_1841.name: Maacah
maachah_1841.who: Favored wife of King Rehoboam and mother of King Abijah, later removed as queen mother for idolatry.
key: Rehoboam loved her above his other wives and made her son Abijah chief prince (2 Chronicles 11).
Her son Abijah reigned three years over Judah (1 Kings 15).
King Asa removed her as queen mother for making an abominable Asherah image (1 Kings 15).
Asa cut down her image and burned it at the brook Kidron (2 Chronicles 15).

mahli_1889.name: Mahli
mahli_1889.who: Levite son of Merari, ancestor of the Mahlite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Merari, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Mahlites were one of the Merarite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).
His sons were Eleazar and Kish; Eleazar's daughters married Kish's sons (1 Chronicles 23).
Sherebiah, a man of discretion from Mahli's descendants, joined Ezra's return (Ezra 8).

mary_1940.name: Mary the mother of James
mary_1940.who: Follower of Jesus, mother of James the younger and Joses, who witnessed his crucifixion, burial, and empty tomb.
key: She watched Jesus' crucifixion from a distance with other women from Galilee (Matthew 27).
She saw where Jesus' body was laid in the tomb (Mark 15).
She came with spices to anoint Jesus' body and found the stone rolled away (Mark 16).
An angel told her Jesus had risen, and the risen Jesus met the women (Matthew 28).
She was among the women who told the apostles about the empty tomb (Luke 24).

matthew_1971.name: Matthew
matthew_1971.who: Tax collector, also called Levi, whom Jesus called to follow him and appointed one of the twelve apostles.
key: Jesus saw him at the tax booth and said to follow him, and he did (Matthew 9).
He held a great feast where Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners (Luke 5).
Jesus chose him as one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10).
After Jesus' ascension, he prayed with the other apostles in the upper room (Acts 1).

menahem_1996.name: Menahem
menahem_1996.who: Son of Gadi who seized Israel's throne by killing Shallum and paid tribute to Assyria.
key: He struck down Shallum in Samaria and reigned in his place (2 Kings 15).
He attacked Tiphsah brutally because it would not open its gates to him (2 Kings 15).
He paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver, taxed from wealthy Israelites (2 Kings 15).
He did evil for ten years, and his son Pekahiah succeeded him (2 Kings 15).

micah_2055.name: Micah
micah_2055.who: Son of Mephibosheth and great-grandson of Saul, through whom Saul's family line continued.
key: Mephibosheth, whom David cared for, had a young son named Mica (2 Samuel 9).
As son of Merib-baal, he fathered Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz (1 Chronicles 8).
His line is listed again in Saul's genealogy among those living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).

molech_2104.name: Molech
molech_2104.who: A pagan god associated with child sacrifice.

mushi_2116.name: Mushi
mushi_2116.who: Levite son of Merari, ancestor of the Mushite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Merari, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Mushites were one of the Merarite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).
His sons Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth are listed in David's Levite divisions (1 Chronicles 23).
His descendants were assigned by lot among the Levites (1 Chronicles 24).

peleg_2308.name: Peleg
peleg_2308.who: Son of Eber, in whose days the earth was divided; an ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus.
key: He was named Peleg because in his days the earth was divided (Genesis 10).
He fathered Reu at thirty and lived 209 years more (Genesis 11).
He is listed in the genealogy from Shem to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).
He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).

queen_of_sheba_2379.name: Queen of Sheba
queen_of_sheba_2379.who: Foreign queen who traveled to Jerusalem to test Solomon's wisdom and praised the LORD for him.
key: Hearing of Solomon's fame, she came to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10).
Overwhelmed by his wisdom and court, she blessed the LORD who set Solomon on Israel's throne (1 Kings 10).
She gave Solomon gold, spices, and precious stones, and he gave her all she desired (1 Kings 10).
Her visit is recorded again in the Chronicler's account of Solomon (2 Chronicles 9).

salah_2455.name: Shelah
salah_2455.who: Descendant of Shem and father of Eber, listed in the line from Noah to Abraham and in Jesus' genealogy.
key: He is listed among Shem's descendants as the father of Eber (Genesis 10).
He fathered Eber at thirty and lived 403 years more (Genesis 11).
He is listed in the genealogy from Shem to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).
He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the son of Cainan (Luke 3).

sheba_2570.name: Sheba
sheba_2570.who: Benjaminite son of Bichri who led a revolt against King David and was beheaded at Abel of Beth-maacah.
key: He blew a trumpet, declaring Israel had no portion in David, and Israel followed him (2 Samuel 20).
Joab pursued him and besieged him in the city of Abel of Beth-maacah (2 Samuel 20).
On a wise woman's advice, the city cut off his head and threw it to Joab (2 Samuel 20).
